newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil ends lower on quiet European veg oil mark.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil ends lower on quiet European veg oil mark.

text.p: Palm oil remained weak at the close of the European vegetable oil market on Monday with prices hit by talk of higher than expected Malaysian output during February.
Traders said no figures were available yet, but some players were saying production had picked up quicker than expected after the long Chinese and Moslem holidays in Malaysia during February.
There was also talk that the Pakistan private sector players were in the market as resellers, putting prices under further pressure, but traders were unable to pin the rumours down.
Lower Chicago prices at the end of last week and at the opening this afternoon were another bearish factor in the market.
European traders said they viewed the Malaysian Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) data for January, released on Saturday, as neutral.

PORLA put production during January at 576,967 tonnes, 9.57 percent down from December. Exports were put at 551,665 tonnes against 652,874 tonnes in December while stocks were 696,272 tonnes against 794,454.
At the close of business crude palm oil cif Europe was $7.50 to $10 down after Mar traded at $570 and $567.50 a tonne cif.
Among products RBD palm oil was $5 to $7.50 down while olein was $7.50 to $10 lower with no further business reported during the afternoon.
Lauric oils finished a tradeless day with sellers unchanged to $2.50 lower.
In soft oils only one trade was reported when May/Jul soy oil fetched 101.25 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
Closing sellers were mixed with soy and rape oil 0.50 guilders up to one guilder down.
